edits.old: For measurement-level deletes whose predicate does not apply to the whole bucket document, MongoDB unpacks candidate buckets, checks each measurement against the delete predicate, and writes surviving measurements back under the original bucket `_id`. A predicate that applies to the whole bucket can skip unpacking and delete the bucket directly. SERVER-99527 explains that a partial delete can recalculate `control.min` while leaving the timestamp embedded in `_id` unchanged, which can affect subsequent query-based bucket reopening. (high confidence)

SERVER-99527 explains that a partial delete can recalculate `control.min` while leaving the timestamp embedded in `_id` unchanged, which can affect subsequent query-based bucket reopening. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-99527

statements.statement: Measurement-level deletes unpack candidate buckets, check each measurement against the predicate, and write survivors back under the original bucket _id.
A predicate that applies to the whole bucket can skip unpacking and delete the bucket directly.
SERVER-99527: a partial delete can recalculate control.min while leaving the _id timestamp unchanged, affecting query-based bucket reopening.
statements.note: Jira description (fixed in 7.0.16, 8.0.4, 8.1.0-rc0) mentions control.min and unchanged _id timestamp.

edits.rationale: The server README describes unpacking, predicate checking, repacking under the same _id, and skipping unpacking when the predicate applies to the whole bucket. SERVER-99527 states that measurement deletes recalculate bucket min/max time while the _id-embedded timestamp stays unchanged, which can let query-based reopening violate the max bucket span.
